chunks: (5) Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtah narrated: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq an-Nahawandi narrated: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated from Sabah al-Muzni, from al-Harith ibn Hasirah, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said: I heard Ali (peace be upon him) saying:

"It is as if I see the non-Arabs setting up their pavilions in the mosque of Kufa, teaching people the Quran as it was revealed." I said: "O Commander of the Faithful, is it not as it was revealed?" He said: "No, the names of seventy from Quraysh have been erased from it, along with the names of their fathers. And Abu Lahab was left only to show contempt for the Messenger of Allah, because he was his uncle."

key_terms.بِأَسْمَاءِ آبَائِهِمْ: along with the names of their fathers

ai.seo_question: What changes were made to the Quranic text regarding the names of Quraysh according to Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Nu'mani, Imam Ali (AS) foretells a time when non-Arabs will recite the Quran in Kufa, asserting that while the text is preserved, the names of seventy Qurayshi families were erased. Notably, the name of Abu Lahab was retained not merely as a record but as a deliberate 'insult' (idhra') to the Prophet, highlighting the theological nuance of divine preservation versus human editorial choices in the Uthmanic codex.
